subject: GST/VAT reverse-charge treatment for platform & seller-fee split
messages:
From: Ayesha Khan <billing@archway.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-08T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question on GST reverse-charge for platform fees and seller split

Hi Mina,

Quick question from our finance team — Archway sells subscription access to our marketplace where we facilitate third-party sellers. We saw platform fees line on the Redwood invoice and want to confirm tax treatment. For EU sales where the buyer is VAT-registered, do you apply reverse-charge on the entire invoice or only on the seller-share? Internally we're trying to map whether the platform fee is considered a taxable supply from Redwood to Archway (our company) or a collection on behalf of the seller.

Attached is our VAT certificate and a sample invoice for May. Can you confirm what evidence Redwood needs to treat the fees as reverse-charge (self-billed) and whether you can split the invoice so the seller portion shows separately for our reclaiming?

Thanks — we need this for our month-end close.

Best,
Ayesha Khan
Billing Lead, Archway Software
attachments: archway-vat-cert.pdf, sample-invoice-may.pdf
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ayesha Khan <billing@archway.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-08T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on GST reverse-charge for platform fees and seller split

Hi Ayesha — thanks for flagging this and for the VAT cert.

Short answer: we can support reverse-charge treatment, but we need to confirm two things to get accounting right:
1) Which legal entity is the billed customer on your account (Archway EU entity or global HQ)?
2) Whether Archway wants Redwood to self-bill the seller-share (we can produce a split invoice / self-billing schedule) or you prefer us to issue a single consolidated invoice with a breakdown line.

Operationally we typically require: a copy of the buyer VAT ID (you provided), evidence of seller VAT IDs for any self-billed seller lines, and a signed self-billing agreement if Redwood will issue seller-level self-billed invoices. I attached a quick self-bill template and our recommended tax code matrix for platform vs seller-attributable fees.

I looped in Ben from Billing to confirm how this will flow in our invoice system and whether we can automate the split for month-end.

Next steps: Ben will confirm what we can do in the short term (June invoices) vs plan for a system change. If you can confirm the preferred option (split self-bill vs consolidated with breakdown) we can draft the self-billing agreement.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
attachments: self-bill-template.xlsx, platform-fee-tax-matrix.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ayesha Khan <billing@archway.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-08T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on GST reverse-charge for platform fees and seller split

Thanks Mina / Ayesha — adding the operational detail.

We can support two viable flows: 

Option A — Self-bill split (preferred for reclaim clarity):
- Redwood issues a primary invoice to Archway for the platform fee (our supply to you).
- Redwood issues self-billed lines for each seller-share that are explicitly marked as self-billed/reverse-charge where applicable.
- Requirements: signed self-billing agreement (simple addendum), seller VAT IDs on file, documentation trail saved to the invoice record.
- Impact: allows Archway to reclaim VAT cleanly; requires a one-time config and manual backfill for May if needed.

Option B — Consolidated invoice with breakdown:
- Single invoice to Archway with line-level description showing gross seller amounts and platform fee retained.
- We apply reverse-charge only on the portion that represents a taxable supply to Archway (usually the seller-share when the seller is the supplier).
- Simpler to implement immediately but less neat for seller reclaim; may require additional ledger notes.

For June close we can do Option B as a stop-gap and target Option A for July after the self-billing agreement is signed. To implement Option A by July 1 we need: signed agreement from Archway, seller VAT ID list (CSV), and confirmation of which sellers you want self-billed vs those that remain directly billed.

I'll start a short ticket with Finance to add the split-line template and flag invoices for July. Marissa — can you approve the temporary consolidated approach if Archway needs a quick fix this month?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Billing Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@archway.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-09T07:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on GST reverse-charge for platform fees and seller split

Hi Ben / Mina — appreciate the options. Archway prefers Option A (self-bill split) for audit clarity. We can: 
- Sign the self-billing addendum (please send as DocuSign).
- Provide a CSV of active seller VAT IDs by EOD Thursday.
- For May and June, we'd like Redwood to provide a short backfill report so our accounts team can reconcile and reclaim where applicable.

Attaching our company VAT cert (same as Ayesha's), and a link to our DocuSign workspace where you can drop the addendum: https://www.docusign.com/archway/self-bill/xyz123

Can you confirm target dates for: (1) the signed agreement in DocuSign, (2) the July self-bill roll-out, and (3) the backfill report for May/June?

Thanks — Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Finance, Archway Software
attachments: archway-vat-cert.pdf
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Question on GST reverse-charge for platform fees and seller split

Tom / Ayesha — thanks, this all looks good and we can proceed with Option A. Summary and timeline below: 

Action items (Redwood):
- I will upload the self-billing addendum to DocuSign today and route to Tom for signature (target: 48 hours).
- Ben will prepare a backfill report for May/June showing seller-level amounts and tax treatment and deliver by Friday 2025-06-13.
- Finance will enable the July 2025 invoice split. July invoices issued 2025-07-01 will include self-billed seller lines where seller VAT IDs are provided.

Action items (Archway):
- Provide seller VAT ID CSV (EOD 2025-06-12).
- Sign DocuSign addendum when it arrives (target within 48 hours).

Notes / exceptions:
- If any seller does not provide VAT ID, we will default to consolidated treatment for that seller until evidence is provided.
- We will store the VAT evidence and signed addendum in the invoice record for audit.

I'll follow up with the DocuSign link once uploaded. Marissa — please confirm the operational go-ahead to schedule the July split.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
